title: Lead record
description: One row of the lead sheet. Written by the Apps Script capture endpoint (integrations/scorecard-capture.gs) from the visitor's own submission; scores are written onto the same row when the card is completed. THE HEADERS ARRAY IN THAT SCRIPT IMPLEMENTS THIS CONTRACT — change the schema and the script together, in one commit, so the two cannot drift. null means unknown throughout; it never means zero.

lead_id.description: The submission_id minted client-side, which is what lets the result find its row.

timestamp.description: Written server-side. A client-supplied time is never trusted.

resource.description: Which asset produced the lead. Needed the moment there are two.

follow_up_opt_in.description: The ONLY consent signal in the system. Set from the visitor's own tick, never inferred, never defaulted, never derived from behaviour. Enforced by automation/lib/consent.mjs, where only the exact string 'yes' passes.

total_score.description: null until the card is completed. 0 means someone scored zero on twenty statements — a different fact entirely.

weakest_signal.description: One category, or a tie recorded as a tie. A tie is never resolved to a winner.

completed_at.description: null if the card was never completed, which is normal and common.

email_sequence_status.description: Mirrored from the email provider, which is authoritative. null means we do not know — not 'not sent'.

discovery_call_clicked.description: null means not instrumented. false asserts we watched and they did not click. Those are different facts and must not be merged.

dwell_ms.description: Spam signal. A submission faster than 1500ms is not a human filling in two fields.

spam_reason.description: Rejected submissions are written WITH a reason rather than dropped, so a false positive is visible rather than invisible.
